de.title: Phrasal Verbs im Alltag (2)
de.intro: Sechs häufige Phrasal Verbs mit ihrer wichtigsten Bedeutung.

cards.back: sich gut verstehen, miteinander auskommen. „I get along well with my colleagues.“

cards.front: look forward to: Was heißt es, und was folgt darauf?
cards.back: sich freuen auf. Danach folgt ein Substantiv oder die -ing-Form: „I look forward to seeing you.“ Nicht: „to see“.
aufschieben, verschieben („We put off the meeting“). Auch: abschrecken, die Lust nehmen („It put me off swimming“).
zufällig treffen („I ran into an old friend“). Auch: auf ein Problem stoßen.
kaputtgehen, ausfallen („The car broke down“). Auch: scheitern (Verhandlungen) oder in Teile aufgliedern („break down the numbers“).
ein Thema ansprechen („Don’t bring up politics“). Auch: ein Kind großziehen.

en.title: Phrasal Verbs in Daily Life (2)
en.intro: Six common phrasal verbs with their most important meaning.

cards.front: get along (with): what does it mean?
cards.back: To be on good terms and live or work together without trouble. In German: sich gut verstehen. "I get along well with my colleagues."

cards.front: look forward to: what does it mean, and what follows it?
cards.back: To await with pleasure. A noun or the -ing form follows: "I look forward to seeing you." Not: "to see".

cards.front: put off: what does it mean?
cards.back: To postpone ("We put off the meeting"). Also: to discourage or make someone dislike something ("It put me off swimming").

cards.front: run into: what does it mean?
cards.back: To meet by chance ("I ran into an old friend"). Also: to come across a problem.

cards.front: break down: what does it mean?
cards.back: To stop working ("The car broke down"). Also: to fail (negotiations) or to split into parts ("break down the numbers").

cards.front: bring up: what does it mean?
cards.back: To raise a topic in conversation ("Don't bring up politics"). Also: to raise a child.
